title: release exits 2 when nobody is there to confirm -- the dispatcher's code for an unknown or inactive command, and vc's 0126 arm could not see it
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 by vc, auditing its own 0126 arm in tests/unit/contract.bats, "no handler under lib/cmd exits or returns 2: that code is the dispatcher's (0119, 0126)". The arm scans for a LITERAL `exit 2` or `return 2`. Release passes its code as an argument: step 6 in lib/cmd/release calls `cut_fail 6 "nobody to ask: no terminal, and --yes was not given" 2`, and cut_fail ends `exit "${3:-1}"`. So `bin/devbin release` exits 2 when nobody is at a terminal to confirm and `--yes` was not given, while the arm, green, says no handler does. vc's 0126 change retitles the arm to what it measures.

WHY IT MATTERS. usage-rules.md's exit line gives 2 one meaning, "unknown or inactive", and says "A new refusal takes a NEW code, never a spare one", because otherwise an assertion on 2 is satisfied by either cause. A script running release where release is inactive and a script running it without `--yes` both read 2. 0126 moved infra's could-not-measure off 2 for the same reason.

HOW IT GOT THERE. On purpose, and the purpose was vc's: W4 in ST0007's review asked that "declined" (1) and "could not ask" (2) be different answers, and AC-5.3 says exits 2. That predates 0119 and 0126, which settled 2 as the dispatcher's code alone. releasecut.bats pins it (assert_reached_confirm, and the arms at :790 and :939), ask_person's comment in lib/helpers cites it, and docs/configuration.md:362 and docs/releasing.md:23 say exit 2.

THE AUDIT BEHIND "THE ONE", so the population is named. Every `exit` and `return` under lib/ and bin/ whose code comes from a variable or an argument was read at 940e776 in vc's build clone. The rest carry 0 or 1, or pass a tool's own status through, which is by design. help's 2 for an unknown topic is the dispatcher's own, and it means unknown. Release's step 6 is the one devbin-own refusal on 2 outside the dispatcher.

OPTIONS. (a) Exit 1, as fullcycle and clean already do when nobody is there to ask; the message tells declined apart from could-not-ask, as it does now. This follows 0126, which made an unmeasured domain a failure rather than giving it a code of its own. (b) A new code, 6, "nobody to confirm". It keeps W4's distinction in the code, at the price of a seventh code in the contract. vc recommends (a). A script cannot decline, so the only thing W4's distinction told apart is a person at a terminal saying no, and the message already carries that.

WHAT CHANGES WITH IT: the cut_fail call's code; ask_person's comment; releasecut.bats's assertions; docs/configuration.md:362 and docs/releasing.md:23; and the pointer in contract.bats's arm. AC-5.3's text is superseded, and the supersession is recorded here rather than rewritten, because ST0007 is closed.

## Resolution

Fixed at 129b66f. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. hv chose option (a) on 2026-09-24: release exits 1 when nobody is there to confirm, as fullcycle and clean do, and 2 is the dispatcher's code alone. cut_fail takes no code any more, since step 6 was its only caller that passed one, and its comment says why it exits 1; the release handler's cut comment and ask_person's contract say so too. ask_person still returns 2 for nobody to ask, a function's answer to its caller, and every caller exits 1 for both and says which. Step 6's row carries the distinction W4 wanted, "declined at the prompt" or "nobody to ask", where a person reads it. release.md's exit table, docs/configuration.md and docs/releasing.md say exit 1 and name the row, and contract.bats's literal-2 scan notes that 0130 moved the one site it could not see. releasecut.bats held exit 2 at eleven sites, not three; every "stopped at the confirmation" check now goes through assert_stopped_at_confirm (exit 1, step 6 FAILED, "nobody to ask"), and the declined arm keeps exit 1 with its own words.
- AC-5.3 SUPERSEDED. ST0007's AC-5.3 says release exits 2 when it cannot ask. ST0007 is closed, so its text is not rewritten: this resolution is the record that AC-5.3's exit code is superseded by 0130, and that the "declined" and "could not ask" distinction of W4 now lives in step 6's row rather than in the code.
- ALSO FIXED, IN THE FILE THIS CHANGE EDITS. The arm "a hung query's whole process group is killed ... and no scratch is left (dc's F2)" counted release scratch in the machine's shared TMPDIR, so it failed whenever another run made release scratch at the same moment. It now gives the run a TMPDIR of its own, with the hung query listing that directory as its control; driven both ways under a planter.
- REVIEWS. vc's review: vc, 2026-09-25, approved on hv's ruling, the arms and the evidence below.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. releasecut.bats at bf64442 with this change's arms: 16 of 87 red, every one "want exit 1 at the confirmation, got 2"; the seventeenth was the old scratch arm's race, fixed here. 6 mutants: N01 to N05 killed; N06, moving the ci query's own scratch, survives because it cannot be reached from that arm, where the query runs inside a wait's scratch.
- THE SUITE. All of tests/unit over the nine 0.1.8 changes stacked in landing order on b10dd41 (0139, 0128, 0133, 0130, 0142, 0143, 0144, 0146, 0147), on a clean checkout (head 308cf21), 2026-09-25 11:34:20Z to 12:09:20Z: 1907 of 1907 ok, 0 not ok, no gaps, its 5 skips the suite's declared ones. Main after the landing is byte-identical to that tree outside intent/.
